# jsontext — spec

## Maturity

**Grade:** 2 · S2 E2 A1 H1 P2 · limited by scope (parity), evidence (EXTERNAL, frozen vectors only -- no tools/interop.zig), performance (fastest in the field not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** parity — Go 1.26 `encoding/json`, Rust `serde_json`, CPython `json` string encoding (surveyed 2026-11-08 from their documented behaviour, not by reading their source; the Go and CPython rows re-checked the same day against what Go 1.26.8 and CPython 3.14.4 actually output, see Anchoring and Compared with)

**Audit:** review 2026-11-08 · mutation 2026-11-08 (146/153, 7 eq) · src b58a70254008728f

**Audit detail:** review 2026-11-08 read `src/root.zig` in full with `invalid_utf8` x `ascii_only` x `html_safe` in mind (12 combinations) and found no defect in the writer or the prescan: every control byte is escaped, surrogates are paired, `ascii_only` cannot emit a lone surrogate (an ill-formed surrogate goes through the policy), no truncated sequence is passed through, the U+FFFD placement is per maximal subpart, `utf8Step` never reads past the slice and `depthWithin` handles an escape at the last byte. Two documentation findings (LOW): the `.reject` doc promised "the prefix before the bad byte stays in the writer" while the old code left the unflushed run out (the test pinned `"`); the new code writes the prefix and the doc says so (test pinned to `"ab`). Mutation: 153 schemata mutants in one ReleaseSafe test binary (`JT_MUT=<id>`, `setsid -w timeout -s KILL 20`, baseline first, src copy under `.zig-cache`): every branch of the escape table and its hex digits, the verbatim-table boundaries (0x1F, 0x20, 0x7E, 0x7F, `"` `\` `<` `>` `&`), `utf8Step` (every lead class remap, every second-byte bound both ways, the three length checks, the three failure lengths), `decodeScalar` (every mask and shift), the surrogate-pair maths, each option, the run flush / run restart of each of the five escaping branches, the final flush, the pending-block buffer (full, direct, order, flush, nibbles), and `depthWithin` (string and escape state, `{` and `[` separately, each closer, `>` vs `>=`, the decrement). First run of the pre-audit tests: 9 survivors of 139 — `depthWithin` never cleared the escape flag, ignored `{`, ignored `}`, or reset to zero on a closer (all four real: the old tests only used `[` and one escape shape) → tests added; five equivalents. After the pending-block rewrite (below) one more survivor was real (`put` never flushing on a full block: the test's runs were merged into one long run) → test fixed. Final survivors, all equivalent: `step.len == 3` in the U+2028 test (a well-formed sequence led by E2 is always 3 bytes: the `utf8Step` sweep compares every lead's length with `std.unicode.utf8ByteSequenceLength`), the lead-byte masks of `decodeScalar` (`0x3F` for `0x1F`, `0x1F` for `0x0F`, `0x0F` for `0x07`) and the trailing-byte mask `0x7F` for `0x3F` (the redundant bits are zero on every well-formed lead / continuation byte; proved by the new exhaustive test over all 1,112,064 scalar values, which the mutants pass), and the two write-granularity boundaries of the pending block (`>` for `>=` at exactly 64 bytes / exactly full: the same bytes in the same order, only the number of `writeAll` calls differs, which the API does not promise). The fuzz harness alone kills 77 of the 146 killed mutants (its oracle is semantic, so it cannot see exact spelling such as uppercase hex; the vectors pin that). Tests added: the replay of `testdata/vectors.txt` / `vectors_go.txt` (1231 inputs x 8 option sets + the four `reject` variants, every expected value produced by CPython, Go or the generator's own independent code, see Anchoring), `decodeScalar` over every scalar, `depthWithin` braces / closers / escapes, pending-block ordering over every run length around 64, the fuzz harness. One performance finding, fixed: control-heavy input was 2.0x Go's encoder (the escapes went through `w.print`); the writer now gathers escapes and short runs in a 256-byte block (`Pending`) and writes `\uXXXX` from a table, worst row 2.04x to 0.90x.

## Compared with

Surveyed 2026-11-08 per `SURVEY-PLAYBOOK.md` from documented behaviour; the Go and CPython rows were then re-checked the same day by running Go 1.26.8 and CPython 3.14.4 over 1231 inputs (`tools/gen_vectors.py`, `tools/go_vectors`); serde_json was not run (no Rust toolchain used), its row stays documented-only. Stars and activity not recorded.

| Project | Language | Licence | Stars | Last release / push | What a user notices against this module |
|---|---|---|--:|---|---|
| [Go `encoding/json`](https://pkg.go.dev/encoding/json) — **reference** | Go | BSD-3-Clause | — | Go 1.26 | String encoder escapes `"` `\` controls (`\b` `\f` short forms, lowercase hex, identical to CPython on every input of the sweep), `<` `>` `&` by default (`SetEscapeHTML(false)` turns that off) and **U+2028/2029 always** (observed: 9 of 1231 rows differ from CPython with HTML escaping off, all of them those two); ill-formed UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD **per byte, written as the six-character escape `\ufffd`** (not the raw character; observed: all 886 ill-formed inputs differ from our output, 243 of them still after reading its escape as the character — the per-byte versus maximal-subpart difference); never `\uXXXX` for printable non-ASCII. No ASCII-only mode. |
| [serde_json](https://github.com/serde-rs/json) | Rust | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | — | — | Escapes `"` `\` and controls; non-ASCII verbatim; input is `&str`, so ill-formed UTF-8 cannot occur. No HTML or ASCII-only option. |
| [CPython `json`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html) | Python | PSF-2.0 | — | 3.14 | `ensure_ascii=True` (default) writes every non-ASCII scalar as `\uXXXX` with surrogate pairs and also escapes DEL (observed); `False` leaves them. `json.dumps` takes `str`, so ill-formed bytes need `bytes.decode('utf-8', 'replace')`, which replaces per **maximal subpart** exactly as this module does (checked on 2-, 3- and 4-byte truncations, overlongs, surrogates and F5..FF). Lone surrogates in a `str` are written as-is. No HTML option. |

**Where we are ahead:** an explicit policy for bytes that are not UTF-8 (`replace` per maximal subpart / `escape_bytes` / `reject`), the escape switches of all three libraries (HTML, ASCII-only, plain) in one writer, and a nesting prescan the three do not offer · **Where we are behind:** no streaming `Encoder` object and no `std.json.Stringify` integration (use `std.json.Stringify` for values; this module is for a string that arrives as bytes); no `\uXXXX` for DEL under `ascii_only` (CPython does; Go does not, and DEL is not a JSON control character — see below).

## What this module is, and what it is not

Two pieces of JSON *text* handling that a dozen modules each wrote again: `writeString` / `writeStringContents` (a JSON string literal from arbitrary bytes) and `depthWithin` (bracket depth of a buffer, string-aware, before a parser allocates). It parses nothing, builds no documents, validates no JSON, and does not write numbers, keys or separators (`std.json.Stringify` does). The caller picks the options at compile time (`StringOptions` is a `comptime` parameter), so the default loop that `accesslog` benchmarked is the one `.{}` compiles to.

Not here, by decision:

- **Number formatting, key ordering, pretty printing, object writers.** `std.json.Stringify` owns them. *Never* in this module: it would make it a second JSON library.
- **Escaping DEL (0x7F).** RFC 8259 §7 does not list it; Go and serde_json do not escape it. CPython's `ensure_ascii` does. Not now; if a consumer needs it, add `StringOptions.escape_del`.
- **Lone surrogates.** A Zig `[]const u8` is UTF-8, where a surrogate (`ED A0..BF`) is ill-formed and goes through the `invalid_utf8` policy. There is no WTF-8 mode. Never (no caller has WTF-8).
- **A per-byte U+FFFD policy (Go's).** Refused: the maximal-subpart policy is the Unicode / WHATWG recommendation. The two differ only on a truncated valid prefix; the tests pin the difference.
- **Escaping `/`.** Never written as `\/`; only needed inside `</script>`, which `html_safe` already covers by escaping `<`.

## Performance

`zig build bench-jsontext` (`tools/bench.zig` against `tools/go_bench`, Go 1.26.8 standard library only; always ReleaseFast): `writeString` with default options against `encoding/json`'s string encoder (an `Encoder` with `SetEscapeHTML(false)`, into a reused buffer on both sides), four shapes (ASCII with nothing to escape, valid UTF-8, ill-formed, control-heavy) of 64 B and 4 KiB generated identically on both sides, best of five, batch doubled past 100 ms. Measured 2026-11-08, load average about 3 on 8 cores (`uptime`), ours/Go:

| shape | 64 B | 4 KiB |
|---|--:|--:|
| ascii | 0.26 | 0.50 |
| utf8 | 0.34 | 0.66 |
| ill-formed | 0.50 | 0.80 |
| control-heavy | 0.65 | 0.90 |

Go writes each ill-formed byte as six bytes (`\ufffd`), we write three; the bytes out differ, the work asked of the encoder is the same. History: the first measurement had control-heavy 4 KiB at 2.04x (every escape went through `w.print` and its own `writeAll`); the `Pending` block (escapes and runs under 64 bytes gathered in 256 bytes, `\uXXXX` from a table) took it to 0.90x. The earlier `accesslog` numbers (ASCII hot path 271 ns before the move, 274 ns after) stay valid for the default loop. No Rust encoder was measured; `fastest` is not measured.

## Wire format / algorithm

RFC 8259 §7. The string literal is `"` + contents + `"`. Contents: `"` → `\"`, `\` → `\\`, `0x08 0x09 0x0A 0x0C 0x0D` → `\b \t \n \f \r`, every other byte below 0x20 → `\u00xx` (lowercase hex), everything else verbatim unless an option applies. UTF-8 classification follows Unicode 16.0 Table 3-7 and the maximal-subpart rule of §3.9 (`utf8Step`). `ascii_only` writes a scalar above U+FFFF as the UTF-16 surrogate pair `\ud83d\ude00` (lowercase hex); `html_safe` adds `<`, `>`, `&` (`\u003c`, `\u003e`, `\u0026`) and U+2028 / U+2029.

The scan is table-driven: one lookup per byte for the verbatim set; a well-formed run is handed over in one piece when an escape interrupts. Escapes and runs under 64 bytes are gathered in a 256-byte block on the stack (`Pending`) and written to the writer in blocks, longer runs go straight through after what is pending, so the output order is the call order. Nothing is allocated.

`depthWithin(bytes, max)` is one pass tracking `in_string` / `escaped`; `[`/`{` outside a string increase depth, `]`/`}` decrease it (saturating at 0). It does not validate — the doc comment lists exactly what it accepts.

## Limits and refusals

- `depthWithin` cap is the caller's `max_depth` (a `usize`); the scan is O(n) and uses constant space, so it can be run on a hostile buffer before a parser.
- `.reject` returns `error.InvalidUtf8` after writing the opening quote and everything before the bad sequence (changed 2026-11-08: the old code left out the unflushed verbatim run); the writer is then left with a partial literal. A caller that cannot tolerate that checks first with `std.unicode.utf8ValidateSlice`.
- No consumer-reachable panic: every public function is total on any bytes; the only `unreachable` is in `accesslog`'s wrapper, on an error the chosen options cannot return.

## Anchoring

Frozen vectors, produced by foreign implementations (README DATA / Provenance): `src/testdata/vectors.txt` (1231 inputs, one line each: hex input, valid flag, then the expected output as hex per option set) is written by `tools/gen_vectors.py` (Python 3, standard library only) and `src/testdata/vectors_go.txt` by `tools/go_vectors/main.go` (Go 1.26, standard library only); the test `vectors: replay …` in `src/root.zig` replays both (`.reject` expects `error.InvalidUtf8` exactly when the valid flag is 0). Column by column:

| option set | expected value from | label |
|---|---|---|
| default (`.replace`) | CPython `json.dumps(bytes.decode('utf-8','replace'), ensure_ascii=False)` | foreign |
| `ascii_only` | CPython `json.dumps(…, ensure_ascii=True)`; `-` for the 45 inputs holding DEL (CPython escapes it, we do not) | foreign |
| `html_safe` | Go `encoding/json` `Encoder` with `SetEscapeHTML(true)` over the text CPython decoded to | foreign |
| `ascii_only` + `html_safe` | CPython's ASCII output with `<` `>` `&` replaced by the generator | `own` (composition of two foreign outputs) |
| `escape_bytes` (+ the other options) | CPython's error handler (its maximal-subpart boundaries) with `\u00XX` per byte written by the generator | `own` (a policy of this module; no foreign equivalent) |
| `reject` | derived: error iff CPython's strict decode fails | `own` |
| DEL under `ascii_only` | passes through (RFC 8259 §7 does not list it; Go does the same, CPython does not) | `own` |

The generator asserts the CPython claim the maximal-subpart policy rests on (`E2 82` and `F0 9F 98` are one U+FFFD, `ED A0 80` three, …) and `go_vectors` reports how Go agrees: its output with HTML escaping off equals CPython's on every row except the nine with U+2028/2029 (Go always escapes them), and Go's own per-byte handling of ill-formed input differs from the maximal-subpart policy on 243 inputs (after reading its `\ufffd` as the character). The `ascii_only` values `€`, `😀`, `é` in the older unit test were also read off CPython. `depthWithin` has no foreign anchor (no oracle for a "prescan that does not validate"): it is pinned by tests, a mutation run and an independent depth reference in the fuzz harness. Every option combination is also round-tripped through `std.json` and fuzzed against an independent WHATWG decoder.

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

## Open

- Move the remaining string-escaper copies onto this module (health, openapi, jinja, cbor diag, mcp, jsonshape, framing's `jsonDepthWithin`); until then each keeps its copy. Health's differs: DEL escaped, and a whole string with any ill-formed byte has every byte >= 0x80 escaped (including valid sequences) — `escape_bytes` here escapes only the ill-formed bytes, a deliberate narrowing the health move must accept.
- No independent (second-person) panic review yet: the sweep in the Hardening line was made by the auditing agent and backed by 4,000,000 fuzz seeds.
